title: Automated Catalog Data Normalization
business: E-commerce retailers managing product catalogs from multiple suppliers.
problem: Suppliers submit product titles with inconsistent typos and formatting, causing duplicate entries and search failures.
solution: Use Levenshtein Distance to quantify the edit cost between incoming product titles and existing database entries to identify potential duplicates for manual review.
steps: Extract the existing product title and the new incoming title.
Initialize a matrix where rows and columns represent the characters of the two strings.
Calculate the cost of operations: 0 for match, 1 for insertion, deletion, or substitution.
Compute the final distance value at the bottom-right cell of the matrix.
Flag entries for human verification if the distance falls below a defined similarity threshold.
outcome: Improved catalog consistency and reduced manual data entry errors without requiring exact string matches.
limitation: The algorithm has a quadratic time complexity relative to the length of the strings, which can cause performance degradation when comparing very long text descriptions.
